papers.title: Reducing Batch Makespan for LLM Agent Workloads through Inference-Environment Coordination
papers.problem: Teams running big batches of LLM agent tasks wait long because the model and the task environment take turns idling.
papers.fix: Coordinating the model server and the task environment cut total batch time by 10.4% to 65.0% with scores unchanged.
papers.practicalUseCase: Batch jobs like benchmarks and training runs finish much sooner, so schedule model work and environment work together.
papers.limitation: The tests used two Ling model versions and four benchmarks, so results on other models may differ.

papers.title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations
papers.problem: Fast few-step image and video generators give near-identical results for different random seeds, which kills variety.
papers.fix: Fast student models keep the teacher's total variation but squeeze it into fewer directions, and ReDiverse restores the variety.
papers.practicalUseCase: You can keep fast generation and get varied outputs back, so add a variety fix when you distill a model.
papers.limitation: The fix was tested on image and video distillation benchmarks plus a user study, not on every model type.

papers.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
papers.problem: Nobody knew why LLMs stall when they search for new research ideas, because tests only showed the final result.
papers.fix: Across six LLMs, nearly all progress comes in the first 30 of 100 questions, and models then plateau.
papers.practicalUseCase: Models can judge good ideas they cannot produce, so feed them ideas from outside instead of waiting for better self-generation.
papers.limitation: The game used 200 papers and yes-or-no answers, so real open-ended research may behave differently.

papers.title: Iris-Z: Scaling One Generative Model Past Specialist Geometry Models
papers.problem: Depth estimation stayed with narrow specialist models, while one general image generator was not good enough at it.
papers.fix: One image model, Iris-Z, makes images with depth, estimates depth from photos, and beats specialist models on depth benchmarks.
papers.practicalUseCase: One general model can replace several specialist models, so try a single generator before building a custom depth model.
papers.limitation: The win appears at large scale on established depth benchmarks, and the paper gives no cost comparison.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk are growing fast, but nobody had mapped how they are issued or what sets their size.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk issues from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts and strong security give larger issues; review costs shrink them.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers should pick equity-based contracts and watch review costs, and regulators should add incentives so more Muslim-majority countries take part.
papers.limitation: Data stops at 2022 and shows links between features and issue size, not proof of cause.

papers.title: Examining the Impact of Waqf Literacy on Waqf Behaviour
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Waqf collection stays low, and it was unclear whether better waqf knowledge changes what Muslims actually give.
papers.fix: Among 642 Indonesian Muslims, waqf literacy raised attitude, social norms, control and past behaviour, which lifted intention to give.
papers.practicalUseCase: Waqf literacy drives giving, so waqf groups should teach how waqf works before they ask for donations.
papers.limitation: The sample covers only Indonesia and measures intention to give, not actual donations made.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many Muslim-majority countries still exclude people from banking even as Islamic finance grew, and the causes were unclear.
papers.fix: Across 35 countries from 2005 to 2021, income, schooling, institutions and internet access drive financial inclusion in OIC countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC countries need more spending on digital systems, youth, women and income, so Islamic banks should serve those gaps.
papers.limitation: The study covers 35 countries and a regression method, so it shows links and may miss country detail.

papers.title: Islamic Social Financial Instruments and Sustainable Community Development: Evidence Synthesis on Community Resilience
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Research on zakat, waqf and sadaqah is scattered, so nobody could see how each one helps community resilience.
papers.fix: A review of 93 studies shows zakat gives short-term relief, waqf builds long-term assets, and sadaqah covers flexible emergency needs.
papers.practicalUseCase: Combined zakat, waqf and sadaqah models work best, so charities should use all three with strong governance and digital tools.
papers.limitation: This is a literature review of studies from 2010 to 2025, so it inherits the gaps of those studies.
